summary: LUNA NAV is an interactive 3D concept tool for exploring candidate landing regions near the lunar South Pole. It calculates approximate Sun and Earth geometry for a chosen date, then compares six sample sites using illumination, Earth line-of-sight, and terrain-slope criteria. A 3D lunar globe, local crater-relief view, time controls, and comparison table make the trade-offs visible. The current prototype uses analytical calculations and illustrative site/terrain inputs; it is a visualization and exploration aid, not a flight-certified navigation or landing system.
details:
Planning a lunar South Pole mission involves balancing several conditions that vary by location and time. A site may receive useful sunlight for power while having a poor view of Earth for communications, or its surrounding terrain may be too steep for a safe landing or traverse. Polar illumination is especially sensitive to local topography and the low angle of the Sun.

LUNA NAV presents these factors together so that students, educators, and early mission-design teams can explore how location, date, and mission priorities affect a preliminary site comparison.
